newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to renew Iraqi oil deal, amount unknown.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to renew Iraqi oil deal, amount unknown.

text.p: Turkey's state oil refinery, Tupras, will renew its agreement with Iraq to buy crude oil under the U.N.'s extended oil-for-food deal, company General Manager Husamettin Danis said.
He said the amount of the purchases under the new deal was not known yet.
"We will buy Iraqi oil again. But the agreement has not been signed yet," Danis told Reuters.
"More details of the new deal will come after it has been signed," he said.

He said Tupras, the first company to buy Iraqi crude oil under the first U.N. deal, had bought a total of 1.861 million tonnes of Iraqi oil under the first accord which went into force on December 10 and ended June 7.
The U.N. Security Council unanimously voted on Wednesday for the six-month extension of the deal from June 8 to let Iraq sell oil worth $2 billion to buy food and medicine for its people.
Turkey's previous agreement under first the U.N. deal had envisaged purchases at 75,000 barrels per day.
